title: Three perfect days in Miami: Halloween weekend
dek: Cafecito on Calle Ocho, a closing-day farewell at PAMM, stone crabs and a costume party on Lincoln Road, then a slow Sunday in Coconut Grove as the clocks fall back.

hero.caption: Art Deco hotels along Ocean Drive in South Beach

intro:
Late October is when Miami starts to belong to the people who live here again. Joe's is cracking stone crabs again, the Heat's new season is under way, and the city has the whole of Halloween weekend to dress up for, which it does with real commitment.

This year the holiday lands on a Saturday, so the big nights stack up. On Friday the Heat host the Pacers in an NBA Cup game downtown, while across Biscayne Boulevard the Arsht Center plays *Ghostbusters* with a live orchestra and invites you to come in costume. Saturday belongs to Miami Beach, where **Lincoln Road** turns into a free block party from 5 p.m. to 2 a.m., and to Wynwood, where HalloWYN runs until 3 a.m. Sunday is quieter but full: the Dolphins play the Patriots in the afternoon, the Arsht stages a free Día de Muertos performance, and the Pérez Art Museum says goodbye to Cecilia Vicuña's red wool *Quipu Gut* on its final day.

The plan below gives each day one part of town: Little Havana and downtown on Friday, South Beach on Saturday, Coconut Grove on Sunday. A word on weather: AccuWeather warned on Oct. 23 that showers and high tides could linger in southeast Florida into Halloween, so Saturday keeps a museum in the afternoon and an umbrella in the bag. And remember that clocks go back an hour early Sunday morning, which buys you an extra hour of sleep after the block party.

days.title: Friday: Little Havana and downtown
days.intro: Cuban coffee and dominoes on Calle Ocho, a last look at a famous installation, then courtside noise at the Heat.

stops.name: Versailles
stops.text: Open since 1971 and still the unofficial town square of Cuban Miami, Versailles is where to start. Order a cafecito at **La Ventanita**, the walk-up coffee window, and a guava pastry or croqueta from the bakery next door, or sit down among the mirrors and chandeliers for eggs, palomilla or a Cubano. *Air Mail* called the kitsch something that feels "like an inside joke that only those who don't get it remark upon." The window line moves fast; the bakery is quicker still.

stops.name: Máximo Gómez Park (Domino Park)
stops.text: Take a short cab east along Calle Ocho to Domino Park, where members (the rules say over 55) play under a covered pavilion beside a mural of the leaders at the 1994 Summit of the Americas. You watch rather than play, and the posted rules ban shouting and swearing, so keep it respectful. The Little Havana Walk of Fame stars are around the corner, and Azúcar Ice Cream Company sits across the street if the heat gets to you before lunch.

stops.name: Sanguich De Miami
stops.text: A few blocks west, this Bib Gourmand counter began as a shipping container in 2017 and now fills a narrow green-tiled room. The Cuban sandwich is the reason to come: pork butt marinated for a week in garlic and spices, pressed on bread baked in-house. Add the thick baton-shaped croquetas, or go for the heavier lechón with garlic-cilantro aïoli. It is open daily 10 a.m. to 6 p.m., takes no online reservations, and usually has a line.

stops.name: Pérez Art Museum Miami
stops.text: PAMM sits on the bay in Museum Park. This is the last weekend for Cecilia Vicuña's *Quipu Gut*, fifty strands of red unspun wool, knotted along almost 33 feet, which the artist made for documenta 14; it closes Sunday. Also on view are *Basquiat: Figures, Signs, Symbols* and *John Baldessari: The End of the Line*. Open Friday 11 a.m. to 6 p.m.; adults $18. Verde, the museum's restaurant, is there if you want a drink on the terrace.

stops.name: Tâm Tâm
stops.text: Tam Pham and Harrison Ramhofer's Vietnamese restaurant started as a supper club and now has a Bib Gourmand, a loud happy room near the county courthouse and a karaoke machine hidden in the bathroom. Order the wings in fish-sauce caramel, the smoky lamb with lettuce and bánh hỏi noodles, and the tamarind pork ribs. It opens at 5:30 on Fridays; book on Resy and eat early, because the arena is a short ride away on the free Metromover.

stops.name: Heat vs. Pacers at Kaseya Center
stops.text: The Heat host Indiana in an NBA Cup group-play game, with doors at 6:30 and tip-off at 8. Kaseya Center sits right on Biscayne Bay, a short walk from the Metromover, and the free Metromover gets you home afterward. If basketball is not your thing, the Arsht Center's *Ghostbusters in Concert* starts at the same hour up Biscayne Boulevard.

days.title: Saturday: South Beach for Halloween
days.intro: Art Deco in the morning, stone crabs at lunch, a museum if it rains, and the whole of Lincoln Road in costume after dark.

stops.name: Puerto Sagua
stops.text: A wood-paneled Cuban diner with a counter that has barely changed since it opened in 1962, at the corner of Collins and Seventh. Keep breakfast simple: The Infatuation's reviewer recommends a colada and tostada in the morning, and novelist Ace Atkins, writing in *Garden & Gun*, likes the perico scrambled eggs and the café con leche served with a silver pitcher of coffee. It is a tourist favorite, but it is two blocks from where the walking tour starts.

stops.name: Official Art Deco Walking Tour
stops.text: The Miami Design Preservation League, the group that saved these buildings, runs this tour daily from the Art Deco Welcome Center on Ocean Drive. It takes about two hours and covers roughly a mile and a half of the Architectural District, explaining the pastel façades, eyebrow ledges and neon you'll see all weekend. Adults $50. Book a morning slot through the league's site; we found a 10:30 start listed for this month.

stops.name: Joe's Stone Crab
stops.text: Joe Weiss opened a lunch counter here in 1913 and it has grown into a Miami Beach landmark for locals, politicians and celebrities alike. The season is on, so order the stone crab claws, served cold with mustard sauce, and finish with Key lime pie. On Fridays through Sundays Joe's serves lunch only, 11:30 a.m. to 2:30 p.m., which makes Saturday lunch the move. Book on OpenTable and expect a wait even so.

stops.name: The Bass
stops.text: Miami Beach's contemporary art museum is the rainy-afternoon plan and worth it in sunshine too. New this fall are Yuko Mohri's *Unviolated Imperfection* and Amalia Pica's *Lecturas Posibles*, alongside Sarah Zapata's *Against a State of Malevolence*. It is open Saturday noon to 5 p.m.; general admission is $15. Collins Park and the beach are right outside when you come out.

stops.name: Lucali
stops.text: The Miami branch of the Brooklyn pizzeria has a Bib Gourmand, a wood-fired brick oven at the back and a sidewalk lined with greenery. The order is the 18-inch pie with its thin, lightly charred crust, pomodoro and fresh basil; a half with meatball crumbles or green chili slivers is the classic tweak. It is open until midnight on Saturdays and books on Resy, and it is a short walk south to Lincoln Road.

stops.name: Lincoln Road Halloween Block Party
stops.text: Miami Beach's annual Halloween party takes over the pedestrian mall from 5 p.m. to 2 a.m. The early evening is for families, with trick-or-treating, candy stations and face painting; after dark come live music, performers and DJs, including the Wonderama Band, and more than 17 restaurants and bars along the road run drink specials. It is free and open to the public. Wear the costume; nearly everyone else will.

days.title: Sunday: Coconut Grove
days.intro: Set your watch back, then spend the extra hour in the Grove's gardens, old houses and two of the city's best kitchens.

stops.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
stops.text: James Deering's bayfront villa opens at 9:30 every day except Tuesday, and the cool first hour is the best of it. Deering moved in on Christmas Day 1916; walk the Italian Renaissance gardens to the bay, then go through the villa's European rooms. Preservation work is under way: the Maze and Theater Gardens, some rooms in the Main House and the Swimming Pool Grotto are closed or under scaffolding, so the visit is shorter than usual. Buy timed tickets online.

stops.name: Los Félix
stops.text: Chef Sebastian Vargas's Mexican restaurant holds a Michelin star for cooking built on heritage corn from across the Americas and seafood from nearby waters. On Sundays it opens for a midday service, 11 a.m. to 3 p.m., which is the relaxed way in. The Guide singles out Key West grouper grilled in banana leaf and a griddled corn cake with crab and charred plantains; the wine list leans natural. Book on OpenTable.

stops.name: The Barnacle Historic State Park
stops.text: A few steps down Main Highway, a path through hardwood hammock leads to the oldest house in Miami-Dade still on its original site, finished in 1891 for Coconut Grove founder Ralph Middleton Munroe and raised on wooden pilings near the bay. Entry is $2 on foot. The last house tour of the day starts at 2:30 and takes ten people, at $3 for adults, so arrive a little early to claim a place.

stops.name: Ariete
stops.text: Michael Beltran's dim, leafy restaurant keeps its Michelin star in the 2026 guide, blending new American cooking and classic French technique. First-timers should take the tasting menu; the Guide notes the fluke with conch escabeche and the venison tartare with bone-marrow sabayon. On Sundays it opens at 5 and closes at 9, and with the clocks gone back, the evening comes on early. Book well ahead on OpenTable.

stay.name: The Setai, Miami Beach
stay.text: A calm, Asian-inspired hotel near the north end of South Beach with a spa and three infinity pools, which Time Out reported in February was voted No. 11 among U.S. hotels for 2026. It is a walk to the Bass and to Lincoln Road, which makes Halloween night easy.

stay.name: The Betsy
stay.text: A literary hotel on Ocean Drive, with more than 130 curated in-room book collections, a 24-hour library, a writer's room and readings in its underground Bbar. You are in the Art Deco district itself, a short walk from the walking tour's start and from the beach.

stay.name: Freehand Miami
stay.text: A relaxed hotel a block from the beach on Indian Creek Drive, with rooms designed by Roman and Williams, a pool garden and the award-winning Broken Shaker cocktail bar. South Beach nightlife is under a mile away, and the Airport Flyer bus stops nearby.

events.name: Heat vs. Indiana Pacers (NBA Cup)
events.text: An NBA Cup group-play game, early in the Heat's new season.

events.name: Ghostbusters in Concert
events.text: The 1984 film on a big screen with Elmer Bernstein's score played live by a chamber orchestra; costumes encouraged. Tickets from about $29.

events.name: Lincoln Road Halloween Block Party
events.text: Trick-or-treating early, then live music, DJs and drink specials along the promenade. Free.

events.name: HalloWYN 2026
events.text: Wynwood's Halloween block party; free with an RSVP on Eventbrite, with paid VIP packages.

events.name: Last day: Cecilia Vicuña, Quipu Gut
events.text: Final day for Vicuña's knotted red wool installation, made for documenta 14.

events.name: Journey to Día de Muertos
events.text: Calpulli Mexican Dance Company tells a love story that crosses into Mictlán, the Aztec underworld. Pay what you can from $0; RSVP required. Ofrendas, sugar-skull decorating and mariachi before the show.

events.name: Dolphins vs. New England Patriots
events.text: A home game against the division rival; expect heavy traffic north of the city through the afternoon.

know: Clocks go back: daylight saving time ends at 2 a.m. on Sunday, Nov. 1, when clocks fall back to 1 a.m. Your phone will adjust; restaurant bookings and tour times on Sunday are in the new time.

From MIA, the Metrorail Orange Line runs from the airport to Government Center downtown in about 25 minutes (5 a.m. to midnight), and the downtown Metromover is free. For Miami Beach, taxis wait outside baggage claim on the arrivals level; metered fares from MIA have a $15 minimum.
Transit: Metrobus and Metrorail cost $2.25 a ride, and contactless payment caps your spending at $5.65 a day for unlimited rides. That covers the Airport Flyer bus to Miami Beach too.

Weather: AccuWeather's Halloween outlook (Oct. 23) flagged showers and high tides lingering in southeast Florida, with conditions improving into the weekend. Pack a light rain layer and allow for flooded low streets on Miami Beach at high tide.
Sunday traffic: the Dolphins host the Patriots at 4:25 p.m. in Miami Gardens; if you're flying out Sunday evening, leave extra time on the roads toward the airport.
Tipping: 18 to 20 percent at table service is standard. Check your bill first in Miami Beach, where a service charge is sometimes already included.
Halloween night on Lincoln Road runs until 2 a.m. and draws a big crowd; walk or take a cab rather than trying to park.
